doc: Read an application's picture in a terminal: its cells as text, their colours and style, and what drew one.

tools.name: terminal.frame
tools.description: The frame as the terminal shows it: its size in cells, the grid in the interface's pixels, its text a row a line; with `cells`, each cell's grapheme, colours (#rrggbb), style and the node that drew it

cells.description: each cell too, row by row (the text alone when not given)

tools.name: terminal.at
tools.description: What drew a cell: its grapheme, colours and style, and the node that drew it last — its id and path in the interface — with the point in the interface's pixels a pointer there would hit

at.description: [column, row], from 0 at the top left

tasks.name: read-the-screen
tasks.summary: Read what the terminal shows, a row a line

tasks.name: ask-what-drew-a-cell
tasks.summary: Go from a cell back to the node that drew it
